A minor can consent to health care services without a parent or guardian if they are married, emancipated or homeless.
Patients aged 12 and up can consent to outpatient mental health treatments, though inpatient treatments and prescriptions to psychotropic medications still require a minimum age of 15.

The licensed provider can conduct a maximum of six outpatient mental health sessions for minors without parental consent, after which re-evaluation is necessary.
If the attending professional deems the minor mature enough, they can participate in mental health treatment or counseling.
